title: Claim no more than the evidence
statement: Before a study becomes a design rule, check its learners, task and contrast, say how strong its evidence is, and read its effect size as a direction only.
example: One review warned against predicting, for Grade 3 learners, the g=.66 a meta-analysis found for prequestioned information.
detail: A review of the research behind an outside content review (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-devfactory-2026-09-10/analysis-current-courses/RESEARCH-BOUNDARIES.md`, 2026-09-10) checked three clusters against the primary papers and found that a mandatory visible mascot cue, a universal after-reading-only rule and claims on feedback timing and size exceeded the evidence; it labels its own design conclusions inferences for evaluation. An adversarial critique of a course-improvement dossier found effect sizes from general, mixed-age literature listed beside planned changes and asked for a direction-not-magnitude tag wherever one appears (`grade3-reading/artifacts/alpha-read-packager/v2_final_package/docs/V2_MONSTER_DOSSIER.md`). A closing-questions design carries an evidence-status table so that nothing in it is defended on a stronger basis than it deserves, rating retrieval and fading well evidenced, SOLO and threshold concepts frameworks, and choral repetition weak (`grade3-reading/artifacts/feedback-closing-questions-2026-09-24/Closing_Questions_Pattern.txt`). An effect size found elsewhere is not a forecast for your own learners.

evidence.quote: The review contains useful ideas, but its **mandatory visible paw**, **universal after-reading-only rule**, and **feedback timing/size claims** exceed the evidence.
Do not predict a .66 effect for Grade3, general transfer, or a particular tap-to-commit interface.
justify DIRECTION not a v2 number
So that nothing in this spec is defended on a stronger basis than it deserves.
There is no good evidence that saying something in unison builds durable knowledge.
Their work supports investigating different instructional functions; it does not validate three conversational agents working together.
This is a warning to test independent learning, not proof of the same effect in English.
I’d treat the professor/peer appearances as design hypotheses.
**It is an intervention guide, not core instruction.** No IES guide gives a grade 4 Tier 1 recommendation on main idea.
The cited experiment concerns decimals, so transfer to literary analysis is a design hypothesis to test.

The spec (§12) asserts "Teens reject cartoonish or over-praising guides" with no citation. No study found tests teen *rejection* of cartoon guides specifically; the closest (Muniady & Mohamad Ali 2020) tests emotional valence/arousal, not rejection, and is a single small study. Flag this spec line as asserted, not sourced.
**Cervetti — strong preliminary, not settled law.** N = 59, one rural school, on-grade readers, a 3-day intervention, and the comprehension-*questions* measure was null and unreliable (α = .46).
So the routine is well motivated and thinly evidenced as a routine.
